themes.title: Pointers and memory
mainQuestions: Look at the Node struct and pushFront. Explain how a new node becomes part of the list.
Look at the destructor. Explain what happens to each node when list goes out of scope at the end of main.
criteria: Student can describe the node structure and how the next pointer links nodes
Student knows allocated nodes must be freed and where this happens in their code

rubric.text: Says how the link is made: the new node takes the old head as its next pointer before head moves to the new node.
Describes what a Node holds (a value and a next pointer) or that the list is a chain of such nodes.
Says that every node was allocated with new and so must be deleted, or that the memory would leak otherwise.
Describes the loop: save the node in temp, move head along, then delete temp.

themes.title: Edge cases
mainQuestions: Look at removeFront. Explain what happens when it is called on an empty list.
criteria: Student can explain the empty-list check or admits the case is not handled

rubric.text: Says that removeFront checks head == nullptr and returns false straight away.
Says what the caller sees: a false return, with nothing removed and out untouched.

themes.title: Tracing the program
mainQuestions: Trace main from the first pushFront call. What does each print() call output?
Suppose pushFront added new nodes at the end of the list instead of the front. What would change in the output of main?
criteria: Student correctly predicts the printed order and explains why nodes appear in reverse insertion order
Student can reason about how changing the insertion point changes the list order

rubric.text: Predicts the printed output: "1 2 3", then "Removed 1", then "2 3".
Explains why the list reads in reverse insertion order: each pushFront puts the new node at the front.
Says the list would then read 3 2 1, the same as the insertion order (and what would print).
Connects the point of insertion to the order of the list.

fixedFollowUps: Suppose the list is empty when pushFront(5) is called. What do head and the new node's next point to afterwards?
If the destructor were removed from LinkedList, what would happen to the nodes created by the three pushFront calls in main?
How does the caller of removeFront find out whether a node was actually removed?
After removeFront succeeds, what happens to the node that used to be first?
What extra information would pushFront need in order to add a node at the end of the list?
